card.name: Linking words in diuretic and electrolyte-loss mechanisms
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as by, the, its or excessive that come right after a verb like reduce or losing, in sentences explaining how a drug or condition changes salt, potassium or lithium levels through the kidney or gut.

modes.label: Reduce the renal clearance
modes.description: The word after 'reduce' (the, its) just before 'renal clearance' of lithium with diuretics.

card.writes: It seems to push toward words that continue a mechanism of fluid or electrolyte loss, while suppressing water-related words.
card.plain: It fires on the small connecting word in sentences explaining how diuretics or laxatives drain salts or slow lithium clearance.

Thiazides are known to induce hypercalcemia by<< reducing>> excretion of calcium in the urine.
